stem: A company runs a web application whose users sign in through an Amazon Cognito user pool. The application calls a REST API in Amazon API Gateway, and AWS Lambda functions run behind the API. The company must restrict the API so that it accepts requests only from users who signed in to the application. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
keywords: accepts requests only from users who signed in

options.text: Set the API methods to AWS_IAM authorization, create an IAM user with an access key for each customer, and sign each request to the API with that access key.
options.why: [IAM users are granted long-term credentials](../facts/iam-identity-center.md#iam-identity-center-users-get-temporary-credentials), and a key for every customer adds key management and request signing to the application.

options.text: Create a Lambda authorizer that downloads the signing keys of the user pool, validates each token in custom code, and returns an IAM policy.
options.why: It works, but the team writes and maintains token checks, although you can [let Amazon API Gateway validate the token](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-api-gateway-validates-user-pool-token) of the user pool.

options.text: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the API stage, and allow requests only from the IP address ranges of the users of the application.
options.why: An IP address does not show who signed in, and the users connect from changing networks, so the rule does not check the sign-in.
options.misconception: believes that a firewall rule can tell whether a user signed in to the application

options.text: Create an authorizer of the COGNITO_USER_POOLS type for the user pool, enable it on the API methods, and send the user's token in the Authorization header.
options.why: The client sends its user pool token, and API Gateway lets the call through when [the supplied token is valid](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-api-gateway-cognito-user-pools-authorizer), with no code to write.

explanation: API Gateway can check user pool tokens itself: you can [let Amazon API Gateway validate the token](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-api-gateway-validates-user-pool-token) and gate access to the API. The client signs in, sends its token, and the call succeeds when [the supplied token is valid](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-api-gateway-cognito-user-pools-authorizer). The Lambda functions receive requests from signed-in users, and the team writes no token code.
takeaway: An API Gateway REST API accepts Cognito user pool tokens through a user pool authorizer, without custom code.
twin: If the stem said "the client signs requests with identity pool credentials" instead: AWS_IAM authorization, because the users [obtain temporary credentials](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-api-gateway-aws-iam-with-identity-pool) from an identity pool.
say: Put a Cognito user pool authorizer on the API methods; API Gateway checks the token.
